"Coming Out of the Ice" is a book by Victor Herman, an American who was imprisoned in the Soviet Union for many years. The book details Herman's experiences in the Soviet Union, including his imprisonment and survival in the harsh Siberian gulag system.

Victor Herman was an American who traveled to the Soviet Union in the 1930s with his family. He was eventually arrested and spent many years in Soviet labor camps, enduring extreme hardship and brutal conditions. The book chronicles his experiences of survival, persecution, and eventual release.

The memoir is known for its detailed and harrowing account of life in Soviet labor camps and Herman's struggle to survive in extremely challenging circumstances. It provides a firsthand account of the Soviet system of political repression during the Stalin era.
